summary.headline: Garware Hi-Tech Q1 FY27 revenue rose 28% YoY to INR633 crore and EBITDA margin hit a record 30.30%, with FY27 guidance reaffirmed.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR633 crore (+28% YoY), EBITDA of INR192 crore (+56% YoY) at a 30.30% margin, and PAT of INR133 crore (+60% YoY). Management attributed the margin to product mix (Sun Control and high-IR products, architectural share) rather than one-offs, and said Q3 will be seasonally lower. Tariff refunds were excluded from Q1 and about 30-40% had been received by the call date, with the balance expected in Q2. FY27 guidance of over INR2,500 crore revenue and 25% plus/minus 2% EBITDA margin was reaffirmed; management also flagged Middle East shipping disruption that delayed some Q1 volume into Q2.

segments.name: Sun Control Films (SCF)
segments.commentary: About 55% of Q1 FY27 revenue versus 48-50% in FY26; management calls it the largest product. A new robotic SCF line (INR192 crore, about 1,200 lakh sq ft annual capacity) is due for commercial production in H1 FY28.

segments.name: Paint Protection Film (PPF)
segments.commentary: About 20% of Q1 revenue versus about 25% last year. Old PPF line runs near 100%; new line at about 60%. Some volume slipped to Q2 due to a ship stuck at Jebel Ali. Five OEM relationships including M&M.

segments.name: Architectural films
segments.commentary: Management says architectural now exceeds 25% of revenue (vs about 5% earlier, as stated) and is the highest-margin product set on like-for-like basis, per management.

segments.name: Garware Home Solutions (D2C)
segments.commentary: 9 studios operational, target 50 by end FY27. 100% direct-to-consumer; Q1 sales described as very small with no figure given. Management said D2C could exceed INR100 crore.

segments.name: Garware Application Studios
segments.commentary: Network over 250 locations in India; 14 international studios across Middle East and US.

guidance_outlook: FY27 revenue guidance reaffirmed at over INR2,500 crore; EBITDA margin guided at 25% plus/minus 2%. Management said 27-28% looked logical but kept the guidance.
Medium-term revenue CAGR of 15-20%; management indicated about INR3,000 crore by roughly two years out and INR3,500 crore in three to four years.
TPU line (PPF backward integration, about 75% for PPF, 25% for new products) to commission in Q3 FY27; company guides an additional 1.5-2% EBITDA margin after stabilisation in FY28.

Tariff refund: about 30-40% received by call date (July-August), with full refund expected in Q2; management estimated net INR50 crore-plus to the company after sharing with US customers. Excluded from Q1.
Margin seasonality: Q1 and Q2 strong, Q3 lower, Q4 recovers.
capex_capacity: TPU line commissioning in Q3 FY27; management said it could support about INR500 crore revenue potential over three years with possible further capex.
New SCF line (INR192 crore, robotic, about 1,200 lakh sq ft/yr) commercial production expected H1 FY28; management cited INR500-550 crore peak revenue potential for this line.
Management said cash deployment priorities are inorganic growth (under evaluation), more capex for backward and forward integration, and a return-of-capital decision to be announced in coming months.
Over INR700 crore invested in strategic expansions over recent years.
demand_pricing: US e-commerce PPF sales rising; dealer and distributor order flow described as strong in Q1.
Middle East demand described as strong, but supply chain disrupted by war; shipments delayed.
Raw material pass-through: management said direct correlation of consumer product raw material to revenue is about 10-12%, and cost increases are passed to customers through negotiation.
TPU addressable market in India described by management as easily above INR1,000 crore, but it requires market creation.
Antidumping duty recommended by DGTR on TPU-based PPF imports from China.

qa_highlights.question: Is the ~60% gross margin sustainable or will it normalise to 54-55%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there were no one-offs, including tariff refunds. Margin depends on product mix (high-IR Sun Control and architectural). Q1 and Q2 are seasonally strong, Q3 lower, Q4 recovers.

qa_highlights.question: Tariff refund status and balance?
qa_highlights.answer: No refund in Q1. About 30-40% received in July-August, with full refund expected in Q2. Net benefit estimated at INR50 crore-plus after customer sharing.

qa_highlights.question: TPU line margin uplift and FY28 expansion?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance of 1.5-2% margin uplift after the TPU line stabilises. Three TPU products are in the target list; the line is expected to add no material volume in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Current utilisation of PPF capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Old PPF line near 100%; new line about 60%, with volume lost to Jebel Ali shipping delay expected to be recovered next quarter.

qa_highlights.question: Why not grow faster than 15-20%?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the constraint is consumer and authority education and niche product positioning, not top-line demand or capacity; it does not want to commoditise Sun Control.

qa_highlights.question: Where is cash being deployed given INR850 crore balance?
qa_highlights.answer: Priorities in order: evaluate inorganic growth, more capex for integration and reliability, then growth capex. No dividend or buyback was announced; details promised in coming months.

risks_watch: Middle East shipping and war-related supply disruption affecting deliveries and Q2 volume recovery.
Sustainability of 30% EBITDA margin: management said Q3 will be lower, and guidance remains 25% plus/minus 2%.
Tariff refund receipt: balance of about 60-70% expected in Q2; quantum and timing to be confirmed.
Garware Home Solutions execution: 9 studios to 50 by FY27 end, channel partner friction, and the unquantified revenue contribution.
TPU and SCF commissioning timelines (Q3 FY27 and H1 FY28) and ramp-up.
Management did not disclose the Q1 revenue or margin split for D2C, nor geography-wise CPD sales (deferred to IR).
summary.management_tone: Confident and upbeat on results and long-term growth, but guarded on forward margins, which management repeatedly described as conservative. Evasive on specifics (GHS revenue, geography mix, R&D spend beyond a 3-5% range, capital return), often deferring to IR.
key_quotes: There is no, I would say, any item which is exceptional like refunds for tariff or something. It is purely from the performance of the company.
We do not want to do like a commoditized Sun Control.
Garware Home Solutions continues to scale steadily with 9 studios currently operational.
So, of course, we will -- when I said 25%, plus/minus 2%, so 27%, 28% seems to be a very logical number for us.
It is 100% D2C business. It is direct to consumer.
Yes. definitely, I have given you the guidance that in next three to four years, we will be somewhere around INR3,500 crores.
